title: Google and Meta Open-source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
gist: Google, with Meta, open-sourced TorchTPU, a native eager-first PyTorch backend for TPUs that replaces the intrusive PyTorch/XLA path and lets GPU code move to TPU largely by swapping the cuda device and nccl backend. Google reports a 30B model hitting 25.7k tok/s inference on a single TPUv7, Qwen3 MoE 235B training scaled to 8,192 TPUv7 chips, and ~5,000 Hugging Face models tested, lowering the switching cost away from Nvidia CUDA.

insights.claim: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs that runs PyTorch workloads with minimal code changes, supporting eager and compiled execution and distributed computing.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Reducing PyTorch friction on TPUs weakens CUDA lock-in and strengthens Google's position as an alternative AI accelerator supplier.

insights.claim: Migrating a PyTorch workload from GPUs to TPUs with TorchTPU mainly involves replacing the cuda device with tpu and the nccl distributed backend with tpu_dist, or using the torch.accelerator.current_accelerator API.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Near drop-in portability lowers migration costs for buyers weighing Nvidia GPUs versus TPUs.
insights.quote: replacing the cuda device with tpu and the nccl distributed backend with tpu_dist
insights.locator: Specifically, migrating from GPUs to TPUs

insights.claim: Google's earlier PyTorch/XLA route (since 2020) required intrusive source changes to define compilable regions, had severe compile latency, lacked eager mode and lagged on distributed primitives, which TorchTPU's eager-first design is meant to fix.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Past tooling friction explains why TPUs captured less of the PyTorch-dominated market; removing it could shift share.
insights.quote: PyTorch/XLA required intrusive source-code modifications to explicitly define compilable regions, suffered from severe compile-time latency

insights.claim: A Hacker News commenter argued Google should have built native PyTorch support for TPUs much earlier because PyTorch's ecosystem is so rich.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Google's late move suggests TPU adoption was held back by ecosystem rather than hardware.
insights.quote: Google should have done this a long time ago. PyTorch's ecosystem is just so rich.
insights.locator: Commenting on the announcement, Hacker News

insights.claim: TorchTPU's DeferAndFuse hybrid eager/compiled mode is claimed by Google to be 50% or more faster than strict eager while reducing peak HBM memory.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Memory-efficiency gains matter as HBM is a binding constraint on accelerator capacity.
insights.quote: can be 50% or more faster than Strict Eager while reducing peak HBM memory
insights.locator: TorchTPU support three eager execution modes

insights.claim: Google ran a 30-billion-parameter model in standard PyTorch on a single TPUv7 chip at 25.7k tokens/s inference at 5,120 sequence length and 22.4k tokens/s at 10,240; training on four TPUv7 chips reached 5.6k and 4.6k tokens/s respectively.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Published TPUv7 throughput numbers give buyers benchmarks for comparing against GPU alternatives.
insights.quote: On a single TPUv7 chip, inference throughput reached 25.7k token/s at 5120 sequence length

insights.claim: Google scaled Qwen3 MoE 235B training from 1,024 to 8,192 TPUv7 chips with TorchTPU and reported competitive performance-per-dollar for large-scale MoE inference using vLLM.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Price-performance claims on frontier-scale MoE position TPUs as a cost alternative for large inference buyers.
insights.quote: Google reported competitive performance-per-dollar for large-scale MoE workloads using vLLM
insights.locator: Google also conducted experiments using Qwen3

insights.claim: Google tested TorchTPU against about 5,000 Hugging Face models across more than 500 architectures in eager and compiled modes on TPU generations from v5e onward.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Broad model coverage reduces adoption risk for enterprises with heterogeneous model portfolios.
insights.locator: To test TorchTPU's ability to run

insights.claim: Beyond offering TPUs through GCP, Google reportedly sells TPUs to enterprise clients for on-premises deployments, including Anthropic, with Meta potentially following.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Merchant TPU sales would make Google a direct competitor to Nvidia in the accelerator market, and Meta co-developing TorchTPU hints at it becoming a customer.

insights.claim: TorchTPU is early-stage, with a roadmap covering dynamic shapes, compilation performance, operator coverage, reinforcement learning and quantization.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Gaps in RL and quantization support remain adoption hurdles to watch.
insights.locator: TorchTPU is still at an early stage
